hints.title: Recursive Quadrant Ordering
hints.text: Observe the order in which quadrants are visited within each subgrid division.

hints.title: Subdivision Order
hints.text: Each power-of-two square decomposes recursively into top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, and top-left regions in counter-clockwise sequence.

hints.title: Divide and Conquer Structure
hints.text: Recurse on the four sub-regions until reaching unit cells of size 1 by 1, assigning incremental numbers in designated order.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def specialGrid(self, n: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        sz = 1 << n
        grid = [[0] * sz for _ in range(sz)]
        count = 0

        def fill(x1: int, x2: int, y1: int, y2: int) -> None:
            nonlocal count
            if x2 - x1 == 1:
                grid[x1][y1] = count
                count += 1
                return
            midR = (x1 + x2) // 2
            midC = (y1 + y2) // 2
            fill(x1, midR, midC, y2)
            fill(midR, x2, midC, y2)
            fill(midR, x2, y1, midC)
            fill(x1, midR, y1, midC)

        fill(0, sz, 0, sz)
        return grid
```

variables: n: grid exponent producing 2^n by 2^n matrix
complexity.notes: Recursion stack depth is bounded by n.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Manual cell-by-cell placement lacks the clean fractal recursive symmetry.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Divide and conquer avoids intermediate buffer allocation aside from output matrix.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identify the base case and recurrence order across the four quadrants.

from typing import List

class Solution:
    def specialGrid(self, n: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        sz = 1 << n
        grid = [[0] * sz for _ in range(sz)]
        count = 0

        def fill(x1: int, x2: int, y1: int, y2: int) -> None:
            nonlocal count
            if x2 - x1 == 1:
                grid[x1][y1] = count
                count += 1
                return
            midR = (x1 + x2) // 2
            midC = (y1 + y2) // 2
            fill(x1, midR, midC, y2)
            fill(midR, x2, midC, y2)
            fill(midR, x2, y1, midC)
            fill(x1, midR, y1, midC)

        fill(0, sz, 0, sz)
        return grid
